question.text: Fund PPI buys 2 lakh Pre-IPO shares of Company XYZ at INR 200/share. IPO issue price is INR 250/share. What is the discount as % of issue price and the absolute rupee advantage per share?

explanation.text: The Logic: Discount per share = 250 - 200 = INR 50. As % of issue price = 50/250 = 20%. Matches PDF Example 10.8 methodology (they compute discount as % of IPO issue price, not of invested amount). The Trap: Options A, D miscompute percent. C misstates absolute advantage. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C same. XV tests valuation of the discount. Manager's Pro-Tip: When booking Pre-IPO P&L at IPO date, recognise only the portion that is economically realizable after lock-in; apply illiquidity discount (typically 10-15% of the Pre-IPO discount) during lock-in. Over-aggressive day-1 mark-up invites auditor pushback.
